title: Understanding the Logistic Regression Model
text: In logistic regression, the decision boundary is determined by the equation of the form: \( \beta_0 + \beta_1 $$x_1$$ + \beta_2 $$x_2$$ $$=$$ $$0$$ \). Given that the threshold \( T $$=$$ $$0.75$$ \) corresponds to \( \sigma(\log(3)) \), we can use this information to find the line equation.

title: Relating the Threshold to the Decision Boundary
text: The threshold \( T $$=$$ $$0.75$$ \) implies that the probability of the positive class is $$0.75$$ when the linear combination of features equals \( \log(3) \). This means that \( $$2x_1$$ + $$3x_2$$ $$=$$ \log(3) \).

title: Finding the Slope \( $$m$$ \)
text: To find the slope \( $$m$$ \) of the line \( $$x_2$$ $$=$$ $$mx_1$$ + $$b$$ \), rearrange the equation \( $$2x_1$$ + $$3x_2$$ $$=$$ \log(3) \) to the form \( $$x_2$$ $$=$$ $$mx_1$$ + $$b$$ \).
